45-day holdout explorer

Every hour of the reported holdout, actual against predicted. Four models forecast 24 hours ahead from a fresh origin each night, so the 45 days tile the window exactly once — no overlap, no gaps, and no model ever saw the day it is predicting.

Mon 9 March – Wed 22 April 2026 (45 days) · 24 tanks · 1,080 hourly points per model · point forecasts are raw (uncalibrated), so the four are directly comparable

Hover or focus the chart and use ←/→ to read any point. In the daily view, click a day to open its 24 hours.

Table view — every value on screen ()

How to read it. Each point is a forecast made before the fact: the origin is 23:00 the night before, the horizon is the next 24 hours. Daily points are matched-pair sums — the actual and every prediction are summed over exactly the hours whose meter reading exists — so a partial day cannot flatter one model. Coverage below 100% is called out in the tooltip and in the table; the headline MAE, MAPE and bias skip points under 95% coverage, which is why the campus outage on 25 March and the gap on 16 March do not count against anyone.

Provenance. Chronos-2 ZS, NPTS and TimesFM 2.5 come from results/chronos2/calibrated/predictions_calibrated.parquet; PatchTST from results/chronos2/holdout45_patchtst/predictions_holdout45_patchtst.parquet. All four share the origin grid. The two fitted models (NPTS, PatchTST) share the fit cutoff (2026-03-08 23:00); the two foundation models (Chronos-2, TimesFM) are zero-shot, with their context cut at each origin — so nothing leaks. TimesFM carries the last observed value across a sensor gap that reaches the origin, where Chronos-2 masks it; that is why it overshoots the day after the 16 March outage. Rebuild with python reports/build_holdout45_page.py.
